policy: Labels describe only hydrologic context explicitly supported by the cited official source. They are not pixel masks and do not set paleoriver=true/false.

labels.rationale: USGS documents a long paleohydrologic history for the Death Valley–Searles Lake system. This confirms paleohydrologic context, not a specific channel mask in this test bbox.
USGS describes Lake Bonneville as a vast Pleistocene lake in northwestern Utah. The label confirms the paleolake basin context, not a mapped paleochannel.
ESA identifies the Ebro river corridor in an arid regional setting. It is retained as an active-river analogue, not as a paleoriver positive label.
ESA documented exceptionally low water in the Po River in 2022. This is a confirmed active-river low-water analogue, not paleochannel ground truth.
ESA notes evidence of water erosion from a wetter climatic period in the Tanezrouft Basin. The source supports ancient water-erosion context but not a pixel-level paleochannel mask.
ESA identifies the Tsauchab as an ephemeral river ending in the Sossusvlei basin. This confirms the modern ephemeral drainage context only.
NASA Earth Observatory documents Lop Nur as a terminal lake whose location and extent changed over time. Specific paleochannels remain unlabelled in this dataset.
ESA documents long-term Aral Sea shrinkage associated with river diversion. The label confirms terminal-basin change, not a paleochannel mask.
